external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: Engineer who opens and uses the dispatch console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: Single-page JavaScript application used by duty engineers to interact with the dispatch API and receive live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: Corporate host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: API in the production control plane used by the console and schedule importer; it reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.notes: The API answers the console cross-origin. The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: Hourly importer that pulls and parses the scheduling partner's SOAP XML feed and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token to the dispatch API. The token has not been rotated since it was issued when the importer was built.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: Database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or the session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: Folder where the importer writes each downloaded scheduling document.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_stores.name: corporate file store
data_stores.description: Corporate file store containing the schedule archive folder.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store

data_flows.name: load console
data_flows.description: Duty engineer loads the dispatch console from the corporate web host.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: Duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: Dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and the API are served from different origins. The API answers the console cross-origin. The allowed origins and credential setting were not recorded.

data_flows.name: open WebSocket
data_flows.description: Dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: It is unknown whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after opening.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: Dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull SOAP feed
data_flows.description: Schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's planned-work feed hourly.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: It is unknown how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: XML document containing tomorrow's planned work

data_flows.name: write archive
data_flows.description: Schedule importer writes each downloaded scheduling document to the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: Schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The importer presents an API token. That token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Network on which duty engineers sit and the schedule importer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: Same-company zone holding the live estate, where an account can move a crew or change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: A corporate laptop holds none of the control-plane rights. The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: Zone controlled by the scheduling partner, which is another company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database's data classification is confidential.
assumptions.basis: The database contains crew names and mobile numbers, as well as tokens or sessions, which are personal data and credentials.
